## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vedanāttika* ("Triad of Feelings") is a structural section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Nyanatiloka 2007]. It forms one of the primary twenty-two triads (*tika*) analyzed in the conditional methodology of the *Paṭṭhāna*, specifically treating the conditional relationships of phenomena associated with feeling [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Structurally, it follows the uniform Abhidhamma matrix of conditional exposition divided into repetitive analytical chapters, such as the dependent chapter (*paṭicca-vāra*), condition chapter (*paccaya-vāra*), supported chapter (*nissaya-vāra*), conjoined chapter (*saṃsaṭṭha-vāra*), associated chapter (*sampayutta-vāra*), and the detailed investigation chapter (*pañha-vāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral identifies no direct cross-canonical parallels for the text [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus identifies massive Pali-internal text reuse (19,710 matching passages across 143 Pali texts), consisting of shared Abhidhamma conditional matrices and permutational formulas [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal textual parallels occur in adjoining Paṭṭhāna chapters, particularly the preceding *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2), *Pītittika* (Patthana 1.8), *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13), and its corresponding section in the later books such as the *Vedanāttika* of Patthana 13.2 [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns formulaic passages with non-Theravāda scholastic works in Sanskrit and Tibetan—including Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta*, Asaṅga's *Yogācārabhūmi*, the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*—representing shared pan-Buddhist analytical classifications of feelings and conditional terminology rather than direct textual lineage [DharmaNexus].
